payload.summary: Reviewed all four amendments against the invariants.rs and shrimp.rs source code. Three amendments identify real gaps (missing egg-cohort sum invariant, unbounded maturation_accum, missing population conservation test) and are accepted. The fourth (fr-2-81a07e81) is rejected because its core claims are factually incorrect: maturation_accum IS reset to 0 when count hits 0 (shrimp.rs:602-606, :662-664), and condition_index IS continuously smoothed toward the global target regardless of stage population (shrimp.rs:307-317). The proposed fix of blending condition_index on recruitment would be semantically wrong since condition represents environmental quality applied uniformly, not individual animal state.

votes.rationale: Confirmed by reading invariants.rs:42-44 and the spawning/egg_development logic. clamp_berried_to_adults (biology.rs:548-554) only trims cohorts when berried > adults — it does not verify sum(egg_cohorts[*].count) == berried_females_count. The legacy migration path (shrimp.rs:465-476) also creates cohorts based on berried_females_count without verifying pre-existing consistency. trim_egg_cohorts trims from the back by excess = berried - adult.count, but if sum(cohorts) was already < berried_females_count (e.g., from save corruption), the mismatch persists and berried females without corresponding egg cohorts will enter the legacy path and generate phantom juveniles on resolution. Adding a one-line repair after line 44 — reconciling berried_females_count to sum(egg_cohorts) — closes a real defensive gap.

Confirmed by tracing the accumulation path in juvenile_to_subadult (shrimp.rs:624-641) and subadult_to_adult (:682-700). When funding fails: accum starts at X, adds count*daily_rate, subtracts candidate_maturing, then re-adds unfunded_maturing (= candidate_maturing when funding is 0), netting out to X + count*daily_rate each tick. This grows linearly and unboundedly under chronic resource shortage. While candidate_maturing is bounded by count (line 627/686) so behavior is ultimately correct, values above count carry zero semantic information — they just waste floating-point precision and create a serialization liability. The clamp maturation_accum = maturation_accum.min(count as f64) is safe (never changes observable behavior since candidate is already bounded by count) and makes the state strictly cleaner.

Reviewed all existing tests in crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_population.rs. They cover spawning, hatching, reserve funding, mortality under stress, and field non-negativity — but none assert the global accounting identity total_count_change == total_births - total_deaths over a multi-day run. This identity is the fundamental invariant of the stage-structured model and would catch exactly the class of phantom-birth or dropped-count bugs that amendments fr-2-6fdbcb32 and fr-2-81a07e81 are concerned about. A dedicated conservation test tracking juvenile additions from hatching, promotions between stages, and mortality counts over 30+ ticks is high-value and straightforward to implement.

The amendment's core claims are contradicted by the existing code. (1) maturation_accum IS properly reset: both juvenile_to_subadult (shrimp.rs:602-606) and subadult_to_adult (:662-664) set maturation_accum = 0.0 and return early when count == 0. So when a stage empties and later receives entrants, the accum is already 0 — new arrivals do NOT inherit stale fractional progress from an extinct cohort. (2) condition_index IS continuously updated: update_condition (shrimp.rs:307-317) smooths all three stages toward a shared global target every tick regardless of count, so an empty stage's condition tracks environmental quality and is not stale when animals arrive. (3) The proposed fix of count-weighting or reinitializing condition_index on recruitment would be semantically incorrect — condition represents environmental quality applied uniformly to a stage, not per-animal health. Blending source and destination conditions on promotion would conflate the environmental condition model with an individual-health model. For the non-empty destination case (existing sub_adults + new promotees), the residual maturation_accum from existing animals is at most fractional (< 1.0 under normal operation) and its impact is negligible (at most one extra promotion one tick early). This does not justify the complexity of a count-weighted blending mechanism.
